content.title: About
content.content: Black beans and white rice is a classic combination found throughout Latin American, Caribbean, and South American cuisines. Beans provide plant‑based protein, fiber, and micronutrients, while rice supplies quick‑digesting carbohydrates and a light texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans are often called the “queen of beans” for their rich flavor and high antioxidant content.
Together beans and rice form a complete protein, offering all essential amino acids similar to animal protein.
In several countries the dish is a national staple and is served on holidays and celebrations.
The dark color of black beans comes from anthocyanins, which have anti‑inflammatory properties.
Traditionally rice is rinsed several times to remove excess starch and improve fluffiness.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Black beans contain about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins in black beans protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for hemoglobin formation and nerve‑muscle function.

items.title: Energy‑dense rice
items.content: White rice quickly supplies glucose, making it useful after physical activity.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and sprouting lower its level.

items.title: High glycemic index of rice
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar rapidly; people with diabetes may prefer whole‑grain rice or control portions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: A small percentage of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas production
items.content: Beans can cause flatulence; proper preparation (soaking, thorough cooking) mitigates this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook beans and rice together in a 1:2 ratio, adding spices, vegetables, or meat. They are used in salads, casseroles, soups, and as a side dish. Soak dry beans at least 6 hours before boiling until tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 1 year. Cooked beans and prepared rice keep 3–4 days in the refrigerator and up to 3 months in the freezer.
